title: 410. Why does everyone have a diagnosis these days?

sentences.en: This is an iHeart PodcaSt.

sentences.zh: 真人保证。

sentences.en: I've been approaching my health really differently this year.
sentences.zh: 我今年对待健康的方式真的很不一样。

sentences.en: I used to be really focused on maximizing and doing more.
sentences.zh: 我以前非常专注于追求极致和做更多的事情。

sentences.en: And now I'm just realizing that if I listen to what my body needs, I perform way better.
sentences.zh: 而现在我只是意识到，如果我倾听身体的需求，我的表现反而会好得多。

sentences.en: And that's why I am obsessed with my WHOOP.
sentences.zh: 这就是为什么我迷上了我的WHOOP手环。

sentences.en: Truly, you guys, you know I'm such a data and information-driven person.
sentences.zh: 真的，伙计们，你们知道我是那种极其依赖数据和信息的人。

sentences.en: And I love opening my WHOOP app and seeing how my sleep, my stress, my strain is correlating with my mood, with my running performance, with how I'm just feeling day-to-day.
sentences.zh: 我喜欢打开WHOOP应用，看我的睡眠、压力、身体负荷与我的情绪、跑步表现以及日常状态之间是如何关联的。

sentences.en: I'm not an elite athlete by any means, but I do really benefit.
sentences.zh: 我绝对算不上什么顶尖运动员，但我确实受益匪浅。

sentences.en: And I also just really enjoy knowing more about my body.
sentences.zh: 而且我也真的很喜欢更多地了解自己的身体。

sentences.en: And WHOOP also gives me these actionable, personalized insights that have made me more intentional and meant that I make smarter decisions
sentences.zh: WHOOP还为我提供这些可操作的、个性化的见解，让我变得更有意识，这意味着我能做出更明智的决定，

sentences.en: day-to-day about what I need rather than just putting my foot on the gas and just going, going, going, going.
sentences.zh: 在日常生活中根据自己的需求做出调整，而不是像踩满油门一样一味地狂奔、狂奔、狂奔。

sentences.en: Hello, everybody.
sentences.zh: 大家好。

sentences.en: I'm Gemma Spake, and welcome back to The Psychology of Your 20s, the podcast where we talk through the biggest changes, experiences, moments, and transitions of our 20s
sentences.zh: 我是珍娜·斯派克，欢迎回到《你二十岁的心理学》，在这个播客里，我们探讨二十岁时面临的最大改变、经历、时刻和转折，

sentences.en: and what they mean for our psychology.
sentences.zh: 以及它们对我们心理意味着什么。

sentences.en: Hello, everybody.
sentences.zh: 大家好。

sentences.en: Welcome back to the show.
sentences.zh: 欢迎回到节目。

sentences.en: Welcome back to the podcaSt.
sentences.zh: 欢迎回到播客。

sentences.en: It is, as always, so great to have you here back for another episode and back for a very big, big episode for us today.
sentences.zh: 一如既往，很高兴你能回来收听新的一期节目，这对我们来说也是非常重要的一期节目。

sentences.en: Today we are talking about a major, pretty huge discussion happening in society at the moment, whether that's online, whether it's in the medical community,
sentences.zh: 今天我们要讨论的是社会上当前发生的一个重大且颇具规模的话题，无论是在线上，还是在医学界，

sentences.en: amongst concerned parent groups, friend groups, policy makers, and that is the idea that everybody has a diagnosis these days.
sentences.zh: 在担忧的家长群体、朋友圈、政策制定者中间，那就是如今每个人都有诊断结果的这种现象。

sentences.en: I'm sure you have heard it.
sentences.zh: 我相信你一定听过。

sentences.en: Everybody has ADHD.
sentences.zh: 每个人都有多动症。

sentences.en: Everybody's anxious.
sentences.zh: 每个人都很焦虑。

sentences.en: Everybody's on the spectrum.
sentences.zh: 每个人都在谱系上。

sentences.en: Everybody could be depressed.
sentences.zh: 每个人都可能抑郁。

sentences.en: Everybody could have OCD, BPD, PTSD, etc.
sentences.zh: 每个人都可能患有强迫症、边缘型人格障碍、创伤后应激障碍等等。

sentences.en: Is this true?
sentences.zh: 这是真的吗？

sentences.en: Is it true?
sentences.zh: 这是真的吗？

sentences.en: Does everybody or could everybody actually have a diagnosis in this day and age?
sentences.zh: 在这个时代，每个人真的都有或者可能有一个诊断吗？

sentences.en: Or is that just public opinion?
sentences.zh: 还是这仅仅是公众的看法？

sentences.en: Is that just public opinion making a problem see, or not even a problem, making a change seem bigger than it is?
sentences.zh: 这只是公众舆论让一个问题——或者甚至算不上问题——让一个变化看起来比实际更大吗？

sentences.en: Is it just increased visibility and reduced stigma that is giving the impression that more people have diagnosed these than before?
sentences.zh: 这仅仅是因为可见度的提高和污名化的减少，才给人一种比以前更多人被诊断出这些疾病的印象吗？

sentences.en: And if numbers are actually increasing, should it be cause for concern?
sentences.zh: 如果数字确实在上升，这是否应该引起担忧？

sentences.en: You know, should we be worried about how other people see themselves or are seen by the medical community?
sentences.zh: 你知道，我们是否应该担心其他人如何看待自己，或者被医学界如何看待？

sentences.en: I have to say a lot of my friends naturally work in the mental health space.
sentences.zh: 我必须说，我的很多朋友自然而然地都在心理健康领域工作。

sentences.en: And this is something that we cannot shut up about because it is so, so, so much more nuanced than what you may read or see online.
sentences.zh: 这是我们滔滔不绝谈论的话题，因为它比你在网上读到或看到的要微妙得多、复杂得多。

sentences.en: It's so much more nuanced than what fear mongering would have you believe.
sentences.zh: 它比贩卖焦虑的言论让你相信的要微妙得多。

sentences.en: So I thought it was time to do this episode, do a whole episode on this topic and like crack open the lid on this discussion.
sentences.zh: 所以我想是时候做这期节目了，围绕这个主题做整整一期节目，并揭开这场讨论的盖子。

sentences.en: I want to thank our researcher Libby as well for her incredible deep dive and diligence with this episode before we even get started.
sentences.zh: 我要感谢我们的研究员利比，在节目开始之前，她为这期节目进行了难以置信的深入研究和严谨的工作。

sentences.en: We also get to talk about one of her papers that she published last year in this episode, which is so exciting that we have somebody working for us
sentences.zh: 我们在这期节目中还会讨论她去年发表的一篇论文，真令人兴奋，我们团队里竟然有人，

sentences.en: who is literally doing the research on this at the same time.
sentences.zh: 同时在做这方面的研究。

sentences.en: So we've got a lot in store.
sentences.zh: 所以我们有很多干货。

sentences.en: Sorry, another disclaimer.
sentences.zh: 抱歉，还有一个免责声明。

sentences.en: It also goes without saying this episode is going to be simply a space for discussion and research and reflection.
sentences.zh: 不言而喻，这期节目将纯粹是一个用于讨论、研究和反思的空间。

sentences.en: It is not for passing judgment.
sentences.zh: 它不是为了评判。

sentences.en: It is not for ending a conversation.
sentences.zh: 它不是为了结束对话。

sentences.en: It is for starting a conversation.
sentences.zh: 它是为了开启对话。

sentences.en: Not everything in this episode will apply to everyone.
sentences.zh: 这期节目中的并非所有内容都适用于所有人。

sentences.en: It may not apply to you.
sentences.zh: 它可能不适用于你。

sentences.en: And you also, you know, you don't have to agree with what we say or everything that we say in this episode if it doesn't actually match your lived experience
sentences.zh: 而且你知道的，如果它实际上不符合你的亲身经历或你所看到的情况，你也不必同意我们所说的话或我们在这期节目中所说的一切。

sentences.en: or what you've been seeing.
sentences.zh: 或者你所看到的情况。

sentences.en: You know, we've done a ton of research to ensure our take on this is balanced.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我们做了大量的研究，以确保我们对此事的看法是平衡的。

sentences.en: But of course, there are nuances that we just like simply can't capture in an hour.
sentences.zh: 但当然，有些微妙之处是我们简单地在一个小时内无法捕捉到的。

sentences.en: So feel free to DM us with your own takes, with your stories, with your experiences.
sentences.zh: 所以请随时给我们发私信，分享你们自己的看法、你们的故事、你们的经历。

sentences.en: If you feel like something is missing, you can also leave a comment if you're listening on Spotify as well.
sentences.zh: 如果你觉得漏掉了什么，如果你正在Spotify上收听，也可以留个评论。

sentences.en: If I don't know if there's something else you want us to include in this episode, but just wanted to put it out there
sentences.zh: 如果我不知道是否还有你想让我们在这期节目中包含的其他内容，但只是想提出来，

sentences.en: that this is obviously an ongoing discussion that society is having.
sentences.zh: 这显然是社会正在进行的持续讨论。

sentences.en: And this is just our small contribution to the conversation.
sentences.zh: 而这只是我们对这场对话的小小贡献。

sentences.en: So without further ado, let's get into the episode.
sentences.zh: 废话不多说，让我们进入正题。

sentences.en: To begin with, before we can even start to dive into this very widespread idea that everybody has a diagnosis these days, we firstly have to actually fact check that.
sentences.zh: 首先，在我们开始深入探讨“现在每个人都有诊断”这一广泛观点之前，我们首先必须核实这一点。

sentences.en: Like, is that true?
sentences.zh: 比如，这是真的吗？

sentences.en: Like our start point here has to be whether the data and the rates of certain conditions are actually increasing.
sentences.zh: 比如我们的起点必须是某些疾病的数据和发病率是否真的在上升。

sentences.en: Because if they're not, like this conversation is kind of nullified, you know.
sentences.zh: 因为如果没有，这个讨论基本上就无效了，你知道的。

sentences.en: We have to actually be able to distinguish between actual numerical shifts and shifts in public opinion.
sentences.zh: 我们必须能够区分实际的数字变化和公众舆论的变化。

sentences.en: This is what the research says.
sentences.zh: 这就是研究显示的内容。

sentences.en: The research says that rates of certain conditions, specifically all forms of depression, all forms of anxiety, have experienced a very, very sharp increase in the last few decades
sentences.zh: 研究表明，某些疾病的发病率，特别是各种形式的抑郁症、各种形式的焦虑症，在过去几十年里经历了非常非常急剧的增长，

sentences.en: with a major increase like during three years after COVID.
sentences.zh: 在新冠疫情之后的三年里更是出现了大幅增长。

sentences.en: Those numbers, they are very easy to see.
sentences.zh: 这些数字非常容易看出来。

sentences.en: It is very easy to look at any, literally any data on this and see that things are tracking up per capita per 100,000.
sentences.zh: 看任何关于这方面的、字面意义上任何数据，都很容易发现情况在按人均、按每十万人计算不断上升。

sentences.en: What you may not know though, is that for other conditions, specifically to do with neurodivergence, the way we actually measure rates can be really confusing.
sentences.zh: 然而你可能不知道的是，对于其他疾病，特别是与神经多样性相关的疾病，我们实际测量发病率的方式可能会非常令人困惑。

sentences.en: So we don't actually and can't actually always have an accurate number, if that makes sense.
sentences.zh: 所以我们实际上并没有也无法总是拥有一个准确的数字，如果这说得通的话。

sentences.en: Like it really depends entirely on which condition you want to talk about and then what kind of rate we're talking about.
sentences.zh: 这完全取决于你想讨论哪种疾病，以及我们讨论的是哪种发病率。

sentences.en: So whether we mean true prevalence, lifetime prevalence, recorded diagnosis, self-diagnosis, medication use, or like wider public conversation,
sentences.zh: 无论是真实患病率、终生患病率、确诊率、自我诊断、药物使用，还是更广泛的公众讨论，

sentences.en: because these things do not rise and fall in exactly the same way as we would typically expect, right?
sentences.zh: 因为这些事情并不像我们通常期望的那样完全同步上升和下降，对吧？

sentences.en: So for example, prevalence rates could be reducing, but medication use could be increasing.
sentences.zh: 所以例如，患病率可能在下降，但药物使用量可能在上升。

sentences.en: So that gives us two different stories.
sentences.zh: 这就给我们讲了两个不同的故事。

sentences.en: Lifetime prevalence could be increasing, but diagnosis rates at the current moment could be staying the same or reducing.
sentences.zh: 终生患病率可能在上升，但当前的诊断率可能保持不变或在下降。

sentences.en: ADHD is probably like the clearest example of why.
sentences.zh: 注意力缺陷多动障碍（ADHD）可能是最明显的例子，说明了为什么。

sentences.en: It is actually hard to pinpoint like how many people are experiencing this, are diagnosis rates going up?
sentences.zh: 实际上很难明确究竟有多少人在经历这种情况，诊断率是在上升吗？

sentences.en: I will say like numerically, they have risen.
sentences.zh: 我要说的是，从数字上看，它们确实上升了。

sentences.en: There has been a huge increase in adult diagnoses between 2000 and 2018, in UK data, US data, Australian data, Canadian data.
sentences.zh: 根据英国数据、美国数据、澳大利亚数据和加拿大数据，在2000年至2018年期间，成人的诊断量有了巨大的增长。

sentences.en: Prescribing has also risen in several countries.
sentences.zh: 几个国家的处方开具量也在上升。

sentences.en: I think in the UK, there's been a 51% increase in patients being prescribed medication over the last five years.
sentences.zh: 我认为在英国，过去五年里开具药物的患者人数增加了51%。

sentences.en: But that is not the only part of this picture.
sentences.zh: 但这并不是全貌。

sentences.en: A 2025 systematic review looking at post-2020 ADHD prevalence actually found no actual conclusive evidence of a real rise in underlying prevalence.
sentences.zh: 一项2025年的系统评价研究了2020年后的ADHD患病率，实际上并未发现底层患病率真正上升的确凿证据。

sentences.en: So what that means is that even though diagnosis, assessment demand, prescribing has clearly increased, essentially when these researchers looked at 40 plus studies,
sentences.zh: 这意味着，尽管诊断、评估需求、处方量明显增加，但本质上当这些研究人员查看了40多项研究时，

sentences.en: they concluded that actually underlying that prevalence probably hasn't changed.
sentences.zh: 他们得出结论，实际上在这背后，患病率可能并没有改变。

sentences.en: It's just that people are showing up for services.
sentences.zh: 只是人们开始寻求服务了。

sentences.en: It's just that they are using the correct language for what they've always been experiencing.
sentences.zh: 只是他们正在为自己一直以来的经历使用正确的语言。

sentences.en: It's just that they are getting help.
sentences.zh: 只是他们正在获得帮助。

sentences.en: They're also getting later stage diagnoses.
sentences.zh: 他们也得到了更晚期的诊断。

sentences.en: These individuals probably should have been diagnosed a lot earlier.
sentences.zh: 这些人本应该早得多得到诊断。

sentences.en: It's only now that they are counting, but the underlying prevalence has always probably been the same.
sentences.zh: 只是现在他们被统计进去了，但潜在的患病率可能一直都是一样的。

sentences.en: Autism tells a very similar story.
sentences.zh: 自闭症也讲述了一个非常相似的故事。

sentences.en: Actual diagnosis rates have risen over time.
sentences.zh: 实际的诊断率随时间推移而上升。

sentences.en: There's been an eightfold increase in the UK over the last 20 years.
sentences.zh: 在过去的20年里，英国的患病率增加了八倍。

sentences.en: But again, much of the literature suggests this is not because of some sudden biological epidemic.
sentences.zh: 但同样，大量文献表明这并不是因为某种突发的生物学流行病。

sentences.en: You know, some people would want you to believe that, that it's vaccines, that it's pesticides, whatever.
sentences.zh: 你知道，有些人希望你相信这一点，认为那是疫苗，那是杀虫剂，诸如此类。

sentences.en: It's not that.
sentences.zh: 不是这样的。

sentences.en: It's rising recognition.
sentences.zh: 这是因为认知度提高了。

sentences.en: It's improved identification amongst population groups that used to be missed,
sentences.zh: 这是因为在过去容易被忽略的人群中识别能力得到了改善，

sentences.en: especially girls and especially people of colour.
sentences.zh: 特别是女孩，尤其是深色皮肤的人群。

sentences.en: That is like also combined with a reduced stigma, which is meaning that people feel more accepted to have this part of them be given a label.
sentences.zh: 这也结合了污名化的减少，这意味着人们觉得把他们身上这一部分贴上标签会得到更多人的接受。

sentences.en: We really need to examine this because historically, diagnostic stereotypes have been really, really narrow.
sentences.zh: 我们真的需要审视这一点，因为从历史上看，诊断的刻板印象一直非常非常狭隘。

sentences.en: For a very long time, many diagnoses were simply shaped around a very limited template of what the typical person with the condition looked like.
sentences.zh: 很长一段时间以来，许多诊断只是围绕着对该典型患者长相的极其有限的模板来塑造。

sentences.en: And often that template was based on the people who were most visible, most disruptive, most easy to identify, or most represented in research.
sentences.zh: 而且通常这个模板是基于那些最引人注目、最具破坏性、最容易识别或在研究中最具代表性的人。

sentences.en: That usually meant we based our entire idea of what a mental health condition or what neurodivergence looked like based on just the population group
sentences.zh: 这通常意味着我们将我们对心理健康状况或神经多样性长相的全部看法，建立在仅仅那一类人群的基础之上，

sentences.en: that happened to be studied firSt.
sentences.zh: 而那一类人群碰巧是最先被研究的。

sentences.en: I cannot overstate how narrow the clinical definition used to be because of that.
sentences.zh: 由于这个原因，我怎么强调过去临床定义的狭隘都不为过。

sentences.en: Because for the first 30 to 40 years of ADHD research, for example,
sentences.zh: 因为例如，在ADHD研究的前30到40年里，

sentences.en: 98% of the people who were being studied were boys under the age of 18.
sentences.zh: 98%被研究的人都是18岁以下的男孩。

sentences.en: And so the definition or the understanding we have or have had in the past has been formed on that.
sentences.zh: 因此，我们过去拥有或已经拥有的定义或理解就是基于此形成的。

sentences.en: Most of the first tests on medications that were used for ADHD, medications that are still used now,
sentences.zh: 大多数针对ADHD药物的最初测试，这些现在仍在使用的药物，

sentences.en: that the basis of those medications are still active in medications we take now for ADHD.
sentences.zh: 这些药物的基础在如今我们为ADHD服用的药物中仍然有效。

sentences.en: Those original tests were exclusively done on boys and men.
sentences.zh: 那些最初的测试完全是在男孩和男性身上进行的。

sentences.en: And so for years, the dominant image has been of the hyperactive little boy who couldn't sit still,
sentences.zh: 因此多年来，主流形象一直是一个坐立不安、多动的男孩，

sentences.en: who interrupted constantly, who ran around, who was obviously very much struggling in ways that inconvenienced other people,
sentences.zh: 不断打断别人，四处奔跑，显然在很大程度上以给其他人带来不便的方式挣扎着，

sentences.en: people, and which were probably very, very confusing for him and everybody involved.
sentences.zh: 这种挣扎对他以及所有相关的人来说可能都非常非常令人困惑。

sentences.en: The issue is, is that this image, it's not incorrect.
sentences.zh: 问题是，这个形象并非不正确。

sentences.en: It's just not entirely correct.
sentences.zh: 它只是不完全正确。

sentences.en: It's just not, it's just not reliable.
sentences.zh: 它只是，它只是不可靠。

sentences.en: It's just one image of one kind of person.
sentences.zh: 它只是某一种人的一个形象。

sentences.en: And that makes it harder to recognize people whose difficulties looked quieter, whose difficulties looked more internal or more socially acceptable,
sentences.zh: 这使得人们更难认出那些困难看起来更安静、更内向或更被社会接受的人，

sentences.en: especially if they had been fundamentally conditioned because of their race or because of their gender to behave differently.
sentences.zh: 特别是如果他们由于种族或性别而从根本上被规定要表现得不同的话。

sentences.en: You know, the example a lot of people give now is like a girl who daydreams and forgets things and procrastinates and is sensitive and feels overwhelmed
sentences.zh: 你知道，现在很多人给出的例子就像是一个会做白日梦、丢三落四、拖延、敏感、感到不知所措的女孩，

sentences.en: and has these, has a really elaborate imagination,
sentences.zh: 并且有着非常丰富的想象力，

sentences.en: probably previously wouldn't have been diagnosed with ADHD, but perhaps that's what she was, what she was going through.
sentences.zh: 她以前可能不会被诊断为ADHD，但也许这就是她一直在经历的事情。

sentences.en: Or, you know, a child of color in like a primarily white community may have been corrected more from an early age,
sentences.zh: 或者，你知道，在一个主要由白人组成的社区里，一个有色人种儿童可能从很小的时候起就被更多地纠正过，

sentences.en: you know, by their parents who were trying to keep them safe, keep them safe from standing out, or by teachers or members of the community who made excuses for the white kids,
sentences.zh: 你知道的，由试图保护他们的父母纠正，保护他们免受显眼的影响，或者由老师或社区成员纠正，他们对白人孩子找借口，

sentences.en: but not for them, meaning that their behavior was curtailed, became less obvious, they masked more and they didn't get the diagnosis
sentences.zh: 但对他们不找借口，这意味着他们的行为受到限制，变得不那么明显，他们进行了更多的掩饰，而且他们没有得到诊断，

sentences.en: or weren't seen as having a condition or having a label that they probably did have all along.
sentences.zh: 或者不被认为患有某种疾病或拥有他们可能一直以来都拥有的标签。

sentences.en: So basically, as our understanding expands, we are seeing this reflected in changing numbers.
sentences.zh: 所以基本上，随着我们理解的扩大，我们看到这反映在不断变化的数字中。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 对吧。

sentences.en: As our understanding of masking, as our understanding of conditioning expands,
sentences.zh: 随着我们对掩饰的理解、对条件作用的理解不断扩大，

sentences.en: essentially it means that we are realizing some delays in our recognition of how different conditions show up in different people.
sentences.zh: 本质上这意味着我们正在意识到我们在认识不同病症如何在不同人身上表现方面存在一些滞后。

sentences.en: You know, from the outside, it might look like suddenly there is this epidemic.
sentences.zh: 你知道，从外表上看，可能看起来突然之间爆发了这场流行病。

sentences.en: It is genuinely just a form of social catch-up and essentially we are just bringing people into the fold
sentences.zh: 但这真的只是一种社会追赶的形式，本质上我们只是把人们纳入其中，

sentences.en: and giving people the resources and the understanding that they probably always should have had, right?
sentences.zh: 并给人们他们本该一直拥有的资源和理解，对吧？

sentences.en: And a big contributor to those increase in diagnostic rates that we are seeing is actually a lot of people who are in their 20s and who are in their 30s,
sentences.zh: 而我们看到的诊断率上升的一个重要推动因素，实际上是许多20多岁和30多岁的人，

sentences.en: some of them even in their 40s, who are looking retrospectively at their lives or who are finally kind of recognizing something about themselves and getting help.
sentences.zh: 甚至有些人已经40多岁了，他们正在回顾自己的生活，或者终于开始认识到自己的一些特质并寻求帮助。

sentences.en: So it means that the level has been well below where it probably should have been for many, many years and then the last, let's say, five, ten years.
sentences.zh: 所以这意味着，在很多很多年里，这个水平一直远低于它本该达到的水平，直到最近，比如说，过去五、十年。

sentences.en: It's actually matched all at once where it should have been for 40 years or longer.
sentences.zh: 它实际上是一次性追平了它本该保持40年甚至更久的水平。

sentences.en: I would argue OCD is probably going to go through this in the near future.
sentences.zh: 我认为强迫症（OCD）在不久的将来很可能也会经历这个过程。

sentences.en: You know,
sentences.zh: 你知道的，

sentences.en: our idea of OCD right now is kind of similar to what our idea of autism or ADHD was like maybe 20 years ago, at least our public knowledge of OCD is still very narrow.
sentences.zh: 我们现在对强迫症的看法，有点类似于我们大约20年前对自闭症或多动症（ADHD）的看法，至少公众对强迫症的认知仍然非常狭隘。

sentences.en: A lot of people still imagine OCD as being about cleaning, checking locks, being orderly, liking things neat, but many people with OCD experience really intrusive taboo thoughts.
sentences.zh: 很多人仍然认为强迫症就是关于清洁、检查门锁、井井有条、喜欢整洁，但许多强迫症患者经历的其实是真正的侵入性禁忌思维。

sentences.en: They experience mental rituals, reassurance seeking, repeated checking that happens internally as much as it does externally, and that's not how people often see it.
sentences.zh: 他们会经历心理仪式、寻求安心、在内部和外部同样频繁的反复检查，而这往往不是人们所看到的。

sentences.en: Some people spend years not recognizing their experiences as OCD because it doesn't match the
sentences.zh: 有些人花了几年时间都没有认出自己的经历是强迫症，因为它不符合

sentences.en: cliche, the way that a young girl's experience with ADHD didn't match the cliche back in the day.
sentences.zh: 那种刻板印象，就像当年一个小女孩的ADHD经历不符合那种刻板印象一样。

sentences.en: I know I've spoken about my experience with OCD in the past, but I literally didn't know I had OCD until I was 23 or like 24.
sentences.zh: 我知道我过去曾谈过自己患强迫症的经历，但在我23岁或24岁之前，我真的不知道自己有强迫症。

sentences.en: And I literally, I studied psychology.
sentences.zh: 而且我真的，我学的是心理学。

sentences.en: Like I worked in mental health research and I didn't realize this.
sentences.zh: 就像我在心理健康研究领域工作过，我却没有意识到这一点。

sentences.en: And the reason why was because the description and the way people talked about it was so narrow.
sentences.zh: 原因在于，人们对它的描述和讨论的方式实在是太狭隘了。

sentences.en: Psychologists before this like gave me so many labels for what I was going through.
sentences.zh: 在此之前，心理学家们给我当时的状况贴了无数的标签。

sentences.en: Um, and none of them felt accurate.
sentences.zh: 嗯，而且没有一个让我觉得准确的。

sentences.en: And nowadays it's like so insane to me that it wasn't picked up.
sentences.zh: 现在回想起来，当时没有被诊断出来简直让我觉得太疯狂了。

sentences.en: Like I used to, I think I've talked about this in an episode before, but I used to have to pray in the exact same way every single night.
sentences.zh: 就像我以前——我想我之前在一期节目中谈到过这个——我以前必须在每天晚上以完全相同的方式祈祷。

sentences.en: I did that for like 18 years of my life.
sentences.zh: 我这样做了大约18年。

sentences.en: As a child, I literally used to have to stare at the sun constantly to reassure myself it wasn't going to explode.
sentences.zh: 小时候，我真的必须一直盯着太阳，以此来向自己保证它不会爆炸。

sentences.en: Like I genuinely think I've done permanent damage to my eyes because of that.
sentences.zh: 我觉得自己真的是因为这个对眼睛造成了永久性的损伤。

sentences.en: Like that, that's OCD.
sentences.zh: 就像那个，那就是强迫症。

sentences.en: That was for me a sign of OCD.
sentences.zh: 对我来说，那是强迫症的一个征兆。

sentences.en: And that's just like some examples.
sentences.zh: 这只是其中的几个例子。

sentences.en: So behind every increase in numbers we are seeing in society that for some people may point to an epidemic,
sentences.zh: 因此，在我们社会中看到的每一个数字增长背后，对某些人来说可能指向一种流行病，

sentences.en: for some people may indicate that people are putting it on these, like the stories that like mine are what it's behind this.
sentences.zh: 对某些人来说可能表明人们在装病，像我这样的人的故事才是这一切背后的真相。

sentences.en: It's just individuals who are finally understanding themselves.
sentences.zh: 这只是那些终于开始理解自己的人。

sentences.en: One final point on this, there was, uh, something this other paper I read spoke about
sentences.zh: 关于这一点最后要说的是，我读过的另一篇论文中提到过一件事

sentences.en: that reflects why rates are increasing all of a sudden.
sentences.zh: 它反映了为什么发病率会突然上升。

sentences.en: And that's because the way that stigma has been slowly reduced over the past few decades, not completely, but it's definitely been reduced.
sentences.zh: 那是因为在过去的几十年里，污名化一直在慢慢减少，虽然没有完全消除，但确实减少了。

sentences.en: And that's meant that a diagnosis is no longer scary.
sentences.zh: 这意味着确诊不再是一件可怕的事。

sentences.en: This has allowed people to accept something about themselves or their child, for example, that they may have always known.
sentences.zh: 这让人们能够接受自己或例如他们的孩子身上某种他们可能一直都知道的特质。

sentences.en: This paper in particular discussed how parents that used to be historical examples of parents who actually
sentences.zh: 这篇论文特别讨论了历史上的一些父母，他们过去常常

sentences.en: would avoid getting a formal diagnosis for their child, even though medical advice was very clear
sentences.zh: 避免为孩子获得正式诊断，尽管医学建议非常明确

sentences.en: that this child had ADHD or had autism because they were, you know, concerned about how a label might
sentences.zh: 指出这个孩子患有ADHD或自闭症，因为他们（你知道的）担心标签会

sentences.en: negatively impact their kids or like they had misinformation about how diagnoses were recorded in medical records.
sentences.zh: 对他们的孩子产生负面影响，或者他们对病历中如何记录诊断结果存在误解。

sentences.en: And they thought that that label might get out as they tried to apply for uni or work or went on to do other things.
sentences.zh: 他们认为当孩子申请大学、工作或去做其他事情时，这个标签可能会泄露出去。

sentences.en: And so they felt like it was the right decision to not get their child diagnosed and not perhaps put a barrier in their way that, that was previously like, uh, definitely was a
sentences.zh: 因此他们觉得不给孩子诊断是正确的决定，这样就不会在他们面前设置一道障碍——过去这绝对是一个

sentences.en: barrier, right?
sentences.zh: 障碍，对吧？

sentences.en: Back then the stigma was so intense that, and still is in many ways, but back then, especially they thought that they were doing the right thing.
sentences.zh: 当时的污名化非常强烈，在很多方面现在依然如此，但当时尤其是这样，他们认为自己在做正确的事。

sentences.en: They thought that they were protecting their child from being seen as different.
sentences.zh: 他们以为自己在保护孩子，不让孩子被视为异类。

sentences.en: Slowly over many, many, many years, you know, we have come to realize that somebody is not doomed because they have ADHD or if they have autism or if they have
sentences.zh: 在漫长漫长的岁月里，（你知道的）我们逐渐意识到，一个人并不会因为患有ADHD、自闭症、

sentences.en: depression or anxiety or any number of things, like they live beautiful, full lives.
sentences.zh: 抑郁症、焦虑症或任何其他疾病而注定失败，他们依然能过上精彩、充实的生活。

sentences.en: Like they can do so much that everything, that everybody else can.
sentences.zh: 就像他们能够做到其他人能做的大多数事情一样。

sentences.en: Um, and so although stigma is like not completely eliminated, it has been reduced or replaced as visibility has improved, as services have improved,
sentences.zh: 嗯，所以尽管污名随着能见度的提高、服务的改善、

sentences.en: as acceptance for people's differences has improved as well.
sentences.zh: 以及对人们差异的包容性的提高，并没有被完全消除，但它已经减少或被取代了。

sentences.en: And what that means is again, as people see themselves represented, as people see that getting a diagnosis is not all doom and gloom, naturally
sentences.zh: 这意味着，随着人们看到自己的代表，随着人们看到获得诊断并非世界末日，自然而然地，

sentences.en: increasing prevalence is going to follow that through recognition.
sentences.zh: 随着认知度的提高，患病率的上升也会随之而来。

sentences.en: And I think that is a really amazing thing.
sentences.zh: 我认为这真的是一件了不起的事情。

sentences.en: So that's the first explanation.
sentences.zh: 所以这是第一种解释。

sentences.en: The rise in diagnoses that everybody is seeing and worried about is really just this.
sentences.zh: 每个人都在关注并担忧的诊断率上升，其实就是这么回事。

sentences.en: It's not that these people were previously fine and now they're not.
sentences.zh: 并不是说这些人以前很健康现在不健康了。

sentences.en: It's not that they're faking it.
sentences.zh: 也不是说他们在装病。

sentences.en: It's just that these people have perhaps never been okay.
sentences.zh: 只是这些人可能从来都没有真正好过。

sentences.en: They've previously been missed.
sentences.zh: 他们以前被漏掉了。

sentences.en: They previously were not counted in the recorded rates.
sentences.zh: 他们以前没有被统计在记录在案的比率中。

sentences.en: Now they are.
sentences.zh: 现在他们被统计进去了。

sentences.en: And yes, that is seemingly is happening all at once.
sentences.zh: 是的，这看起来似乎是一次性发生的。

sentences.en: But when you look at that over the period of time that it should have happened.
sentences.zh: 但如果你把这个放在它本该发生的时间跨度来看，

sentences.en: So for example, if you take everybody who is being diagnosed at 12, 15, 27, 47, and you
sentences.zh: 比如，如果你把所有在12岁、15岁、27岁、47岁被诊断的人集中起来，

sentences.en: imagine they all got diagnosed at the same age, you would see that actually rates are not increasing as much as you think.
sentences.zh: 想象他们都在同一个年龄被诊断，你会发现实际上发病率并没有你想象的那么高。

sentences.en: Yes, there's been slight bumps, but actually still prevalence rates are when you view them in that way, uh, remaining pretty consistent with only slight variations.
sentences.zh: 是的，确实有一些轻微的波动，但实际上，当你从这个角度来看时，发病率保持得相当稳定，只有微小的变化。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: When we return, I want to talk about another way that diagnoses or rates of diagnosis for certain
sentences.zh: 当我们回来时，我想谈谈另一种情况：为什么某些特定病症的确诊率或诊断比例

sentences.en: conditions are seemingly increasing because of how the DSM is changing, because of how we categorize certain conditions is changing.
sentences.zh: 似乎在上升，这是因为《精神疾病诊断与统计手册》（DSM）在变，因为我们对某些病症的分类方式在变。

sentences.zh: 我们还将讨论大制药公司和企业所扮演的角色。

sentences.zh: 请不要走开。

sentences.en: To understand why everybody has a diagnosis or it feels that way these days, we also need to understand that diagnostic systems are not written in stone.
sentences.zh: 要理解为什么现在每个人都有诊断结果，或者感觉现在到处都是这样，我们还必须明白，诊断系统并不是一成不变的。

sentences.en: They are revised classifications.
sentences.zh: 它们是经过修订的分类标准。

sentences.en: They are shaped by evidence, cultural debates, cultural norms, clinical needs, and often politics, which I don't
sentences.zh: 它们由证据、文化辩论、文化规范、临床需求以及通常的政治因素塑造而成，我觉得

sentences.en: think I see a lot of people talking about, but politics and cultural context changes how we see certain conditions.
sentences.zh: 好像没多少人谈论这个，但政治和文化背景确实改变了我们对某些病症的看法。

sentences.en: For example, PTSD, that only became a diagnosable condition in the, I think, 1980s
sentences.zh: 例如创伤后应激障碍（PTSD），它直到我想大概在20世纪80年代

sentences.en: after the Vietnam War because all these veterans came home and were lobbying for this condition to be included.
sentences.zh: 越南战争之后才成为一个可诊断的病症，当时所有这些退伍军人回到家乡，一直在游说将这种病症纳入其中。

sentences.en: The removal of homosexuality as a mental condition only happened in 1973, right?
sentences.zh: 同性恋不再被视为一种精神疾病发生在1973年，对吧？

sentences.en: Our clinical guidelines for, and I hate to say this, but like for what is an impairment or not an impairment
sentences.zh: 我们对于——我讨厌这么说，但对于精神上什么是功能受损或什么不是功能受损的

sentences.en: mentally is constantly being revised to actually match what is accurate.
sentences.zh: 临床指南一直在被修正，以真正符合准确的标准。

sentences.en: Like PTSD should always have been in the DSM.
sentences.zh: 就像PTSD本来就应该被收入DSM中一样。

sentences.en: Homosexuality should never have been in the DSM, right?
sentences.zh: 同性恋本来就不应该被收入DSM中，对吧？

sentences.en: And so we are naturally going to see changes in this document as our understanding of people and our understanding of human psychology changes.
sentences.zh: 因此，随着我们对人类以及人类心理的理解不断变化，这份文件自然也会随之发生改变。

sentences.en: So the DSM is the Diagnostic and Statistical Manual of Mental
sentences.zh: 所以DSM就是《精神疾病诊断与统计手册》

sentences.en: Disorders.
sentences.zh: （Diagnostic and Statistical Manual of Mental Disorders）。

sentences.en: I should have said that originally, but it's used for every single diagnosis worldwide by every single mental health professional.
sentences.zh: 我本该一开始就这么说，但全世界的每一位心理健康专业人员都在为每一项诊断使用它。

sentences.en: And the reason we are seeing increases is also because of how the criteria for certain conditions has changed in the DSM.
sentences.zh: 我们看到诊断率上升，也是因为DSM中某些病症的标准发生了变化。

sentences.en: So the first edition of the DSM was published in 1952.
sentences.zh: DSM的第一版于1952年出版。

sentences.en: It included 106 diagnoses.

sentences.zh: 归咎于关于疫苗或环境变化的各种理论，或者他们想归咎于人们是在装病，又或者是在盲目地将一切过度病理化。

sentences.en: I get the fear.
sentences.zh: 我能理解这种恐惧。

sentences.en: It's very scary for people to see this and think that something's going wrong.
sentences.zh: 人们看到这种现象并认为出了什么大问题，这其实是件很吓人的事。

sentences.en: And so they're looking for an explanation.
sentences.zh: 所以他们一直在寻找一个解释。

sentences.en: It's just that the explanation is a lot bigger and is a lot more complicated.
sentences.zh: 只不过这个解释要宏大得多，也复杂得多。

sentences.en: The real explanation is that the reason we are seeing diagnosis rates increase is that criteria are broadening.
sentences.zh: 真正的解释是，我们之所以看到诊断率上升，是因为诊断的标准正在拓宽。

sentences.en: More people are finding the language to describe themselves.
sentences.zh: 越来越多的人找到了能够描述自己状态的词汇。

sentences.en: More people are being identified by mental health systems and being able to self-identify and then get help, which is a good thing.
sentences.zh: 越来越多的人被心理健康系统识别出来，并且能够进行自我识别从而获得帮助，这是一件好事。

sentences.en: A small portion of those people are being misidentified and misidentifying themselves because of concept creep, because of social media.
sentences.zh: 其中有一小部分人因为概念泛化和社交媒体的影响而被错误识别或自我识别错误。

sentences.en: Often those people, like it's very rare those people ever get a formal diagnosis anyways, because it's not like they're just handing them out like candy.
sentences.zh: 通常这类人——这种情况非常罕见，他们其实永远也拿不到正式的诊断，因为诊断可不是像发糖一样随随便便给出的。

sentences.en: The problem with that small amount of people who are getting the wrong diagnosis is firstly that they
sentences.zh: 这一小撮被错误诊断的人所带来的问题，首先在于他们

sentences.en: actually don't get to understand themselves in the correct way, but also that, you know, the pressure that people are claiming that puts on services.
sentences.zh: 无法以正确的方式真正理解自己，同时也是因为，你知道的，人们总说这给公共服务带来了压力。

sentences.en: What I'm really saying is like, if we actually had more funding for services, it wouldn't be a problem, right?
sentences.zh: 我真正想说的是，如果我们能为公共服务提供充足的资金，这根本就不是个问题，对吧？

sentences.en: Because people would get the help they needed, whether that was a diagnosis or not.
sentences.zh: 因为无论是否获得诊断，人们都能得到他们需要的帮助。

sentences.en: Gatekeeping actually helps no one.
sentences.zh: 人为设卡其实对谁都没有好处。

sentences.en: Like we would have a more accurate idea of how many people are dealing with mental health concerns and disorders and conditions.
sentences.zh: 这样我们就能更准确地了解到底有多少人在应对心理健康问题、各种失调以及病症。

sentences.en: Whether that is more or less, we would be able to help more people regardless of whether
sentences.zh: 无论这个数字是多是少，我们都能为更多人提供帮助，而不需要去管他们

sentences.en: they had a diagnosis or not, regardless of what was going on, if we concentrated on expanding mental
sentences.zh: 到底有没有确诊，也不用管具体发生了什么，只要我们把精力集中在扩大心理

sentences.en: health funding, rather than focusing all of our attention on this larger debate about who counts and who doesn't.
sentences.zh: 健康资金上，而不是把所有的注意力都放在这场关于谁算数、谁不算数的宏大争论上。

sentences.en: Does that make sense?
sentences.zh: 这听起来有道理吗？

sentences.en: Because I don't want this to come across as like, A, this isn't a problem, or B, that self-diagnosis is a problem.
sentences.zh: 因为我可不想让大家觉得，A，这不是个问题，或者 B，自我诊断是个问题。

sentences.en: We're just seeing such an uptick in demand because of all these factors and our governments being able to cope with that, not because of the
sentences.zh: 我们之所以看到需求量出现如此惊人的增长，是因为所有这些因素叠加在一起，而我们的政府却无力应对，这并不是因为

sentences.en: people, not because it's people seeking help.
sentences.zh: 人们的错，也不是因为大家都在寻求帮助。

sentences.en: It's not their fault.
sentences.zh: 这并不是他们的错。

sentences.en: It's because they just don't see it as a priority.
sentences.zh: 纯粹是因为政府根本没有把这当作优先事项。

sentences.en: And I think that's where the big problem, just where this all comes down to and why so many people are forced to go looking for the language and forced to go looking for the
sentences.zh: 我认为这才是最大的问题所在，也是这一切的根源，为什么那么多的人被迫去寻找词汇，被迫去独自寻找

sentences.en: explanations by themselves that perhaps gives them a less accurate picture or less access to the
sentences.zh: 解释，这或许让他们只能得到一个不太准确的认知，或者无法获得真正需要的帮助，

sentences.en: help they really need and makes them deal with this like in solitude and without actually somebody there to give them a clearer understanding of themselves.
sentences.zh: 让他们只能孤立无援地面对这一切，身边甚至没有人能给他们提供一个更清晰的自我认知。

sentences.en: Unfortunately, as well, with this huge increase in demand for diagnosis and government systems that can't or won't step up, what we're
sentences.zh: 不幸的是，随着诊断需求的暴增以及政府系统无力或不愿出手干预，我们

sentences.en: also seeing is that private industries are looking to make a buck in this gap in the market.
sentences.zh: 同时还看到，私营资本正试图在这个市场空白中捞取利润。

sentences.en: And the role of these industries cannot be overstated.
sentences.zh: 这些行业所起到的作用绝对不容小觑。

sentences.en: Pharmaceutical companies are obviously the example a lot of us think of because, you know, they do want more people diagnosed by any means possible so that these
sentences.zh: 制药公司显然是我们许多人首先想到的例子，因为，你知道的，他们确实想通过一切可能的手段让更多人被确诊，好让这些人

sentences.en: people become consumers of their medications, right?
sentences.zh: 成为他们药物的消费者，对吧？

sentences.en: There is this documentary, I think it's called
sentences.zh: 有一部纪录片，我想它叫

sentences.en: The Age of Anxiety, and it was made in 2012.
sentences.zh: 《焦虑时代》，拍摄于 2012 年。

sentences.en: And it does an amazing job at investigating how Big Pharma has exploited the increasing demand for mental health support, regardless of what's best for the individual.
sentences.zh: 它在调查大型制药公司如何利用不断增长的心理健康支持需求方面做出了不起的贡献，全然不顾什么对个人才是最好的。

sentences.en: Like they've seen this increasing demand as a money making thing.
sentences.zh: 就像他们把这种不断增长的需求看作是一门赚钱的生意。

sentences.en: Prior to the 1970s, I don't know if you guys know this, there was a greater distinction between medical depression that required
sentences.zh: 在 20世纪 70 年代之前，我不知道大家知不知道，医学上对需要药物治疗的医学性抑郁，

sentences.en: medication and depression caused by circumstances which required more talk therapy or more, you know, life intervention or a mixture of both.
sentences.zh: 与由环境引起的、需要更多谈话疗法或生活干预（或两者结合）的抑郁症之间，有着更明确的区分。

sentences.en: But as pharmaceutical companies began to market anti-depressant drugs, which by the way, I'm on, I'm a big fan of, this is not some conspiracy, but as
sentences.zh: 但随着制药公司开始营销抗抑郁药物（顺便说一句，我自己也在吃，我是个坚定的支持者，这绝不是什么阴谋论），随着

sentences.en: they began to market these drugs, the focus of treatment for many people became more homogenous and it became more medical for everyone.
sentences.zh: 他们开始推广这些药物，许多人治疗的焦点变得更加单一，对所有人来说都变成了一种纯粹的医疗手段。

sentences.en: And that obviously helped these companies make a lot of money because they were able to erase some of the distinctions that are required when it comes to mental health.
sentences.zh: 这显然帮助这些公司赚取了大量的金钱，因为他们得以抹杀了一些在涉及心理健康时本该存在的差异。

sentences.en: Private assessments, private assessment clinics, therapy platforms, self-help brands,
sentences.zh: 私人评估、私人评估诊所、疗愈平台、自助品牌、

sentences.en: wellness apps, supplement companies, productivity tools, coaching industries, all benefit from a
sentences.zh: 健康应用、保健品公司、效率工具、教练行业，都在这样一个文化中获益——

sentences.en: culture where more and more people are encouraged to see themselves as needing an explanation, a label,
sentences.zh: 在这种文化里，越来越多的人被鼓励认为自己需要一个解释、一个标签、

sentences.en: treatment, optimization, management, and less people have access to actual clinical services with people who are trained, with people who could seriously help them.
sentences.zh: 治疗、优化和管理，而与此同时，越来越少的人能够获得由专业人士提供的、真正能够实质性帮助他们的临床服务。

sentences.en: I've seen articles about people being conned out of hundreds, if not thousands of pounds and dollars trying to seek an ADHD diagnosis only
sentences.zh: 我看到过一些文章，讲述人们在试图寻求 ADHD（注意缺陷多动障碍）诊断时，被骗走了几百甚至几千英镑或美元，

sentences.en: for it to not be formally recognized by a regulated healthcare professional.
sentences.zh: 结果却根本不被受监管的医疗专业人员正式承认。

sentences.en: So they actually couldn't even get access to the support and medication that they need anyways.
sentences.zh: 所以他们最终甚至还是无法获得他们急需的支持和药物。

sentences.en: There's all these as well examples of courses for people with anxiety, with ADHD, with OCD that aren't even made by licensed professionals
sentences.zh: 此外还有各种各样的课程，针对焦虑症、ADHD、强迫症患者，甚至都不是由持证专业人士制作的，

sentences.en: because people are like getting into this gap in the market.
sentences.zh: 因为总有人想要钻这个市场空白的空子。

sentences.en: And these courses, I actually was looking at one the other day.
sentences.zh: 而这些课程——我前几天还特意看了一个。

sentences.en: I've just so inaccurate and simplified and just dumb.
sentences.zh: 简直错得离谱、过分简化，而且愚蠢至极。

sentences.en: And this is so incredibly sad because it's like everybody wants to focus on how everybody has a problem these days and diagnoses
sentences.zh: 这真的让人感到无比痛心，因为大家似乎都把焦点放在“现在每个人都有毛病”或者“诊断都是假的”上面，

sentences.en: are fake, but people are really desperate for help and are really desperate to be heard and supported.
sentences.zh: 但人们其实极度渴望得到帮助，极度渴望被倾听和支持。

sentences.en: And when we do not find a good way to meet that demand and to help these people, whether they
sentences.zh: 当我们找不到一个好的方式来满足这种需求、去帮助这些无论是否确诊的人时，

sentences.en: have a diagnosis or not, there are money-making machines that will capitalize on that lack of support.
sentences.zh: 那些唯利是图的赚钱机器就会利用这种支持的匮乏来大发横财。

sentences.en: There is money in framing it this way, and there is money in being able to sell people a solution to their problems through a label.
sentences.zh: 用这种方式来包装它有利可图，通过一个标签把解决方案卖给面临问题的人同样有利可图。

sentences.en: I just think that when there is money involved, we need to be really, really cautious.
sentences.zh: 我只是觉得，只要涉及金钱利益，我们就必须保持极高、极高的警惕。

sentences.en: Again, that does not mean everyone seeking help is being manipulated, is self-diagnosing inaccurately.
sentences.zh: 再次强调，这并不意味着每一个寻求帮助的人都在被人操纵，也不意味着所有人都在不准确地自我诊断。

sentences.en: Absolutely not.
sentences.zh: 绝对不是这个意思。

sentences.en: This doesn't mean that medication is bad or that clinicians are acting in bad faith.
sentences.zh: 这并不代表药物是坏事，也不代表临床医生们怀恨在心。

sentences.en: No, it just means that diagnostic systems don't exist in a vacuum.
sentences.zh: 不，这只是说明诊断系统并不是在真空中运作的。

sentences.en: They exist as part of all these wider factors to do with politics, to do with economics, to do with clinical understanding.
sentences.zh: 它们作为更广泛因素的一部分而存在，这些因素与政治、经济以及临床认知息息相关。

sentences.en: And some of those factors come with incentives, and we need to be aware of that so that we're not acting blindly.
sentences.zh: 而其中某些因素伴随着利益驱动，我们需要对此保持清醒的认识，免得盲目行事。

sentences.en: Some skepticism is healthy, not towards the individuals who are trying to find an explanation and trying to better themselves,
sentences.zh: 带有一点怀疑态度是健康的，这种怀疑不是针对那些试图寻找解释、努力完善自我的个人，

sentences.en: but towards any system that might profit from telling more and more people that their distress is
sentences.zh: 而是针对任何可能从中渔利的系统——它们通过告诉越来越多的人：他们的痛苦

sentences.en: best understood as an internal problem that has a label that can be serviced through a product, a service, or a subscription that only they can sell you.
sentences.zh: 最好被理解为一个内在问题，并且有一个可以通过某种产品、服务或只有它们才能卖给你的订阅来解决的标签。

sentences.en: So this brings me to my final point of the day.
sentences.zh: 这就引出了我今天的最终观点。

sentences.en: With all of this in mind, is it better to over-diagnose or under-diagnose?
sentences.zh: 考虑到这一切，究竟是过度诊断更好，还是诊断不足更好？

sentences.en: This is a huge question to end on, but I want to break it down.
sentences.zh: 这是一个以宏大问题收尾的话题，但我希望能将其拆解开来看看。

sentences.en: Under-diagnosing is what we had in the paSt. And honestly, I think there are large parts of it that are quite tragic.
sentences.zh: 诊断不足正是我们过去常有的状态。说实话，我认为它在很大程度上可以说是相当悲剧的。

sentences.en: It leaves people unseen, unsupported, and blamed for struggles others do not understand.
sentences.zh: 它让人们的痛苦被无视、得不到支持，还要为那些别人无法理解的挣扎背负骂名。

sentences.en: It means people can spend years of their life thinking that they are lazy, thinking that they are difficult, dramatic,
sentences.zh: 这意味著人们可能会花上生命中的好几年，认为自己很懒惰、认为自己很难搞、戏多、

sentences.en: weak, broken, when in reality, they're just dealing with something that has simply never been recognized and that they were never able to have the language to understand.
sentences.zh: 脆弱、破碎，而现实中，他们只是在应对一种从未被认可、也从未拥有词汇去理解的状况。

sentences.en: And that really has, that has consequences.
sentences.zh: 而这确实会带来后果。

sentences.en: Of course, I don't need to say that, but it impacts our self-esteem, our relationships, our finances, the quality of life that we have.
sentences.zh: 当然，不用我说大家也知道，这会影响我们的自尊、人际关系、财务状况以及我们的生活质量。

sentences.en: We do not want to go back that way.
sentences.zh: 我们绝不想走回老路。

sentences.en: We do not want to go back to the under-diagnosis path and make it even harder for people to get help.
sentences.zh: 我们绝不想回到诊断不足的老路上，让人们获取帮助变得更加困难。

sentences.en: Over-diagnosis, though, has its own risks too.
sentences.zh: 然而，过度诊断同样也有它自身的风险。

sentences.en: It can pathologize ordinary human variation without meaning to.
sentences.zh: 它可能会在无意中将普通的人类多样性病理化。

sentences.en: It can pull attention away from the context that we're in that may be describing why
sentences.zh: 它可能会转移人们的注意力，让人忽视我们所处的环境——正是这种环境可能解释了为什么

sentences.en: more people are having severe symptoMs. And it can sometimes lead people towards explanations or treatments that don't actually fit the full picture of them as a person.
sentences.zh: 会有更多人出现严重的症状。它有时甚至会把人们引向那些并不完全契合他们作为一个完整人这一全貌的解释或治疗中。

sentences.en: And that can really blur the line between mild difficulty and profound impact.
sentences.zh: 这确实会模糊轻微困难与深远影响之间的界限。

sentences.en: And when that happens, diagnostic language can start to lose some of its meaning.
sentences.zh: 当这种情况发生时，诊断语言就会开始失去它的一部分意义。

sentences.en: So I don't think it's necessarily better to do either.
sentences.zh: 所以我认为盲目倾向于哪一方都不是最好的选择。

sentences.en: I think that the real goal here is to diagnose well and diagnose carefully, contextually, and with room for an evolving understanding of a person, not just a label.
sentences.zh: 我认为真正的目标应该是：做出良好且谨慎的诊断，结合具体语境，并为不断深化对一个人的理解留出空间，而不仅仅是贴上一个标签。

sentences.en: Like, who is this person?
sentences.zh: 比如，这个人究竟是谁？

sentences.en: Rather than seeing them as having this or that, who are they?
sentences.zh: 与其把他们看作是得了这样或那样的病，不如想想他们是谁？

sentences.en: What are they going through?
sentences.zh: 他们正在经历什么？

sentences.en: What language do they need, label or otherwise?
sentences.zh: 他们需要什么样的词汇，是标签还是其他？

sentences.en: But then what help do they need as well?
sentences.zh: 但同时他们又需要什么样的帮助？

sentences.en: Remember, labels, diagnoses are just clusters of symptoms or patterns of functioning.
sentences.zh: 记住，标签和诊断只是一堆症状或运作模式的集合。

sentences.en: They do not describe a person entirely.
sentences.zh: 它们并不能完全描述一个人。

sentences.en: If you have met one person who has ADHD, one person who has autism, OCD, BPD, anxiety, depression, whatever it may be, you have met one person who is experiencing that.
sentences.zh: 如果你见过一个患有 ADHD 的人，一个患有自闭症、强迫症、边缘型人格障碍、焦虑症、抑郁症或无论什么病症的人，你也就仅仅是见过一个正在经历这种状况的人罢了。

sentences.en: Just one.
sentences.zh: 仅仅一个。

sentences.en: Because it's always going to be different.
sentences.zh: 因为每个人的情况永远都是不一样的。

sentences.en: A label is an oversimplification for a reason.
sentences.zh: 标签之所以存在，就是为了过度简化问题。

sentences.en: Because it needs to oversimplify things so we can categorize people.
sentences.zh: 因为它必须简化事物，我们才能对人群进行分类。

sentences.en: We need to instead be focusing on the person.
sentences.zh: 相反，我们应当把焦点重新聚焦在人本身上。

sentences.en: And I know that might seem like a faraway dream because of the strain that resources and services are currently under.
sentences.zh: 我知道由于目前资源和公共服务所承受的压力，这听起来可能像是一个遥不可及的梦想。

sentences.en: But I think that is like really the problem that we are getting to.
sentences.zh: 但我认为这正是我们正在逼近的核心问题所在。

sentences.en: The system is faulty.
sentences.zh: 这个系统是有缺陷的。

sentences.en: The system is underserving everybody.
sentences.zh: 这个系统没有为任何人提供充足的服务。

sentences.en: I think what that means is that the problem with under versus over diagnosis is being turned into an individual issue to deal with.
sentences.zh: 我认为这意味着，诊断不足与过度诊断之间的矛盾，正被转嫁成一个需要个人去独自应对的问题。

sentences.en: It's turned onto the individual to try and make sense of themselves using whatever resources they have, social media being one of them.
sentences.zh: 这变成了由个人去尝试利用他们手头仅有的任何资源（社交媒体便是其中之一）来搞懂自己。

sentences.en: And we are being increasingly forced to take care of ourselves without the help of somebody who is trained to do so.
sentences.zh: 我们越来越被迫在没有专业人士帮助的情况下照顾好自己。

sentences.en: And again, regardless of whether you have a diagnosis or not, the pressure should be on the system.
sentences.zh: 再说一次，无论你是否确诊，压力本就应该给到系统身上。

sentences.en: It should be on underfunded healthcare systeMs. It should be on the fact that, you know, rush assessments take place all the time.
sentences.zh: 压力应该给到资金严重不足的医疗系统上。应该归咎于这样一个事实，即仓促的评估时刻都在发生。

sentences.en: It takes years to get an assessment for something.
sentences.zh: 仅仅为了某项评估就要等上好几年。

sentences.en: Schools support systems are not good at putting in place healthcare plans or identifying children who could need help.
sentences.zh: 学校的支持系统根本不擅长落实医疗保健计划，也不擅长识别那些可能需要帮助的孩子。

sentences.en: Like I can just go on and on and on.
sentences.zh: 比如我可以一直说个没完没了。

sentences.en: Like the private companies come in and are like, we can make a buck off of making everybody believe that they are not well without actually caring about anybody who is not well.
sentences.zh: 比如一些私企涌入进来，好像在说，只要让所有人觉得自己有病，我们就能大赚一笔，而根本不管那些真正有病的人。

sentences.en: So I just think that's like something to really be conscious of.
sentences.zh: 所以我认为这确实是我们需要真正去注意的事情。

sentences.en: I'm going to finish up this episode with a quick summary of which I've done several, but a proper summary for this topic.
sentences.zh: 我将用一个简短的总结来结束这期节目，虽然我已经做过几次了，但这是针对这个话题的一个恰当的总结。

sentences.en: Why does everybody have a diagnosis these days?
sentences.zh: 为什么现在每个人都有个诊断结果？

sentences.en: Point one, not everybody has a diagnosis these days.
sentences.zh: 第一点，并不是现在每个人都有诊断结果。

sentences.en: Yes, rates are increasing, but they are just catching up to an underlying prevalence rate that has always been there.
sentences.zh: 是的，比例在上升，但它们只是赶上了原本就一直存在的潜在患病率。

sentences.en: For conditions like depression and anxiety, those rates are incredibly high.
sentences.zh: 对于抑郁症和焦虑症这样的情况，这些比例高得惊人。

sentences.en: And that is a real concern.
sentences.zh: 这确实是一个令人担忧的问题。

sentences.en: And that is showing that there is something changing in our society and happening in our society.
sentences.zh: 这表明我们的社会正在发生某些变化，并且正在我们的社会中发生着。

sentences.en: And there have been things happening in our society that are deeply, deeply impacting everybody really.
sentences.zh: 而且我们的社会中一直都在发生着一些事情，对每个人都产生了非常深远的影响。

sentences.en: When it comes to other conditions though, rates do seem to be increasing, but a large majority of this rate increase is coming down to people who previously, historically should
sentences.zh: 不过，当谈到其他情况时，发病率似乎确实在上升，但这种发病率上升的绝大部分原因归结于那些过去、历史上本应该

sentences.en: have been diagnosed, but they were not included by diagnostic criteria.
sentences.zh: 被诊断出来，但却没有被诊断标准所包容的人。

sentences.en: They didn't have the language they weren't seen or their case or the way that they represented didn't match stereotypes.
sentences.zh: 他们没有表达的语言，他们没有被看到，或者他们的病例以及他们的表现方式不符合刻板印象。

sentences.en: Some people are mislabeling normal human idiosyncrasies with catch all inaccurate terMs.
sentences.zh: 有些人正在用包罗万象、并不准确的词汇给正常的个人特质贴上错误的标签。

sentences.en: Sometimes there's coming from social media and other sources, but it is not our job to be concerned with how an individual chooses to see themselves.
sentences.zh: 有时这些来自社交媒体和其他渠道，但我们的工作不是去关注个人选择如何看待自己。

sentences.en: And we should be more focused on ensuring that that person can get in and see a clinician, that person can get help, then we should be at trying to correct
sentences.zh: 我们更应该关注的是确保这个人能够去看临床医生，这个人能够获得帮助，而不是去试图纠正

sentences.en: whether whatever they are experiencing is true or false in our eyes.
sentences.zh: 他们所经历的一切在我们眼中是对还是错。

sentences.en: We also need to be skeptical of a lot of systems around us right now that are trying to make more people feel like something is wrong with
sentences.zh: 我们还需要对我们周围许多目前试图让更多人觉得自己有问题系统保持怀疑，

sentences.en: them, especially when they can make money from it, especially when they seek to gain from the oversimplification of mental health language.
sentences.zh: 特别是当它们能从中赚钱时，特别是当它们企图从心理健康语言的过度简化中获利时。

sentences.en: So make sure that you are looking out for that.
sentences.zh: 所以一定要注意这一点。

sentences.en: Make sure that you are aware of the systems in place that may be manipulating certain parts of of distress or impairment happening in your life.
sentences.zh: 确保你意识到现有的系统可能正在操纵你生活中发生的某些痛苦或受损部分。

sentences.en: But again, it is a really complicated, complicated thing.
sentences.zh: 但再说一次，这是一个非常非常复杂的问题。

sentences.en: And until we have more money and until we have more research and until we have the care towards this and just towards humanity that we actually need, like we're going to continue
sentences.zh: 在我们拥有更多资金、更多研究、以及对这件事情和对全人类真正需要的关怀之前，就像我们将继续

sentences.en: to see this debate, like be very intense and continue to see people perhaps suffering and struggling in ways that they don't really need to.
sentences.zh: 看到这场辩论非常激烈，并继续看到人们可能以并不真正需要的方式遭受痛苦和挣扎。

sentences.en: I'm going to finish it there.
sentences.zh: 我就说到这里。

sentences.zh: 我们做到了。

sentences.zh: 这仍然是一个不断发展的对话。

sentences.zh: 而且我觉得这就像是，这是那种我们只是找不到答案的事情之一。
